canonicalFacts.claim: Early biologic treatment decreases the risk of surgery in Crohn's disease patients.

redFlags: Risk of relapse after anti-TNF withdrawal varies from 20-50% at 1 year and 50-80% beyond 5 years
Patients with IBD have increased risk of colorectal cancer requiring surveillance
Fistula-associated anal carcinoma is a rare but increasingly recognized complication in Crohn's disease

excludedAgents.name: Aminosalicylates
excludedAgents.reason: Cochrane meta-analysis found conflicting results with no clear efficacy for inducing remission or response in mildly to moderately active Crohn's disease

excludedAgents.name: Fructo-oligosaccharides
excludedAgents.reason: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial showed no significant benefit in active Crohn's disease

excludedAgents.name: Rifampicin plus ethambutol
excludedAgents.reason: Two-year randomized double-blind crossover controlled trial showed no significant difference compared to placebo

excludedAgents.name: Sargramostim
excludedAgents.reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial failed to demonstrate efficacy for moderate-to-severe active Crohn's disease

excludedAgents.name: Secukinumab
excludedAgents.reason: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial showed unexpected negative results with potential worsening of disease in moderate to severe Crohn's disease
